notes.1: Many candidates appreciated that sensitivity is a characteristic of living things, although a number incorrectly opted for breathing, perhaps confusing it with respiration.
notes.2: Many candidates understood that the most accurate method of classifying animals is by identifying similarities in DNA base sequences. Some incorrectly believed that identifying similarities in anatomy would be the most accurate method. �PAGE�15
notes.3: This proved to be a challenging question. The number of candidates selecting each option suggests that many candidates were unsure that having two pairs of legs on each segment is a feature of some myriapods.
notes.8: Many candidates understood that the process involved in the uptake of glucose by the epithelial cells of kidney tubules is active transport. Some candidates incorrectly opted for translocation.
notes.10: Many candidates were able to derive the correct answer but some did not seem to realise that the percentage of all the matching bases should add up to 100%.
notes.13: This proved to be a demanding question. Only areas of the leaf that possess chlorophyll would have starch and turn blue-black. The white areas of the leaf would be the same colour as the iodine which is yellow- brown.
notes.14: Many candidates appreciated that it can be concluded from the graph that more stomata are closed during light periods. Some candidates incorrectly concluded that more stomata are closed during dark periods. Candidates need to work carefully through the data to avoid errors in interpretation.
notes.16: This proved to be a demanding question. There was a misconception that sugars dissolve the enamel of the teeth. Bacteria respire the sugar and produce acid, which dissolves the enamel.
notes.17: Some candidates appreciated that water evaporates from the surface of the spongy mesophyll cells and then diffuses out of the stomata.
notes.18: This was a challenging question. Only a few candidates were able to work out that the experiment shows that translocation occurs in the phloem.
notes.19: Many candidates appreciated that the blood vessels that take blood into the heart are the pulmonary vein and the vena cava.
notes.20: Some candidates identified the correct description of angioplasty. The commonest incorrect response was the description of a stent.
notes.21: Most candidates understood that after vaccination, the child produced memory cells.
notes.22: Few candidates appreciated the sequence of changes that take place when we breathe in. Some candidates incorrectly believed that the pressure in the lungs increases at the start of inspiration. The increased volume of the thorax decreases the pressure in the lungs allowing air to flow in from outside. �PAGE�16
notes.23: Only a few candidates appreciated that enzymes are involved in respiration.
notes.24: Many candidates appreciated that deep breathing after exercise reduces an oxygen debt. Some candidates incorrectly believed that the energy in lactic acid is released by anaerobic respiration.
notes.25: Candidates needed to appreciate that at the higher temperature, the student would be sweating more and therefore producing less urine. This item proved to be challenging for many candidates.
notes.32: While many candidates correctly identified the mRNA, some incorrectly believed that it was DNA.
notes.34: Most candidates did not know that during meiosis a diploid cell produces haploid cells that are genetically different.
notes.37: Few candidates were able to correctly identify all the energy transfers through a food chain.
notes.39: Few candidates were able to work out that to determine the answer, the mass of bacteria after five days needed to be multiplied by the mass of protein per gram of bacteria. �PAGE�17
notes.general_comments:
There was good understanding of: levels of organisation; photosynthesis taking place in chloroplasts; the
elements found in proteins and carbohydrates and calculations involving magnification.
There was some uncertainty about: the characteristics of myriapods; the cause of the start of dental decay;
the processes involved in the loss of water from leaves; the pressure changes in the lungs during inspiration
and angioplasty.
It is important for candidates to work methodically through information provided in questions, particularly
those involving graphs.
